tirzepatide.name: Compounded Tirzepatide
tirzepatide.heading: Explore the science behind tirzepatide
tirzepatide.intro: Filter by topic or search to find a study. These trials studied FDA-approved tirzepatide, not compounded versions.

studies.title: Tirzepatide Once Weekly for the Treatment of Obesity
studies.finding: Significant average weight reduction over 72 weeks in adults with obesity or overweight, without diabetes.

studies.title: Tirzepatide as Compared with Semaglutide for the Treatment of Obesity
studies.finding: Head-to-head comparison: greater average weight loss with tirzepatide than semaglutide at 72 weeks.

studies.title: Continued Treatment With Tirzepatide for Maintenance of Weight Reduction
studies.finding: Looked at keeping weight off, and weight regain after stopping treatment.

studies.title: Tirzepatide versus Semaglutide Once Weekly in Patients with Type 2 Diabetes
studies.finding: Greater reductions in HbA1c and body weight with tirzepatide in people with type 2 diabetes.

studies.title: Tirzepatide for Obesity Treatment and Diabetes Prevention
studies.finding: Three-year look at progression to type 2 diabetes in adults with obesity and prediabetes.

studies.title: Tirzepatide for Metabolic Dysfunction–Associated Steatohepatitis with Liver Fibrosis
studies.finding: Improved MASH on liver biopsy in adults with biopsy-confirmed disease.

studies.title: Tirzepatide for the Treatment of Obstructive Sleep Apnea and Obesity
studies.finding: Fewer breathing interruptions during sleep, plus improvements in several other sleep measures.

studies.title: Tirzepatide for Heart Failure with Preserved Ejection Fraction and Obesity
studies.finding: Examined heart-failure events and quality of life in people with obesity-related HFpEF.

studies.title: Effects of Tirzepatide Versus Insulin Glargine on Kidney Outcomes in Type 2 Diabetes
studies.finding: Suggested favorable kidney outcomes compared with insulin glargine.

studies.title: Body Composition Changes During Weight Reduction with Tirzepatide in SURMOUNT-1
studies.finding: About 75% of weight lost was fat mass and about 25% was lean mass.

studies.title: Changes in patient-reported outcomes and objective assessments based on baseline symptom severity in SURMOUNT-OSA: post-hoc analyses
studies.studied: Adults with obesity and moderate-to-severe obstructive sleep apnea in two 52-week placebo-controlled trials, grouped by how tired, sleepy or snoring they were at the start.
studies.finding: Compared with placebo, tirzepatide was linked to larger gains in self-reported sleep and daily function, and people with worse symptoms at the start tended to report bigger gains.
studies.limit: This was a later look back at trial data by subgroup, so the subgroup differences are less certain than the main trial results.

studies.title: Comparative Efficacy of Tirzepatide Versus Semaglutide for Weight Loss in Adults With Overweight or Obesity: A Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis of Head-to-Head Studies
studies.studied: 10 head-to-head studies (41,381 adults with overweight or obesity) that compared tirzepatide with semaglutide for at least 24 weeks.
studies.finding: Tirzepatide was linked to about 4 percentage points more weight loss than semaglutide, but serious side effects were reported more often with tirzepatide.
studies.limit: The pooled studies included observational studies as well as randomized trials, which can make comparisons less reliable.

semaglutide.name: Compounded Semaglutide
semaglutide.heading: Explore the science behind semaglutide
semaglutide.intro: Results apply to the populations studied, and not every studied use is FDA-approved. These trials studied FDA-approved semaglutide, not compounded versions.

studies.meta: 2021 · Wilding et al. · N Engl J Med
studies.title: Once-Weekly Semaglutide in Adults with Overweight or Obesity
studies.finding: About 14.9% average weight reduction over 68 weeks with semaglutide 2.4 mg, versus 2.4% with placebo.

studies.title: Two-year effects of semaglutide in adults with overweight or obesity: the STEP 5 trial
studies.finding: About 15.2% average weight reduction at 104 weeks, versus 2.6% with placebo.

studies.meta: 2022 · Wilding et al. · Diabetes Obes Metab
studies.title: Weight regain and cardiometabolic effects after withdrawal of semaglutide: The STEP 1 trial extension
studies.finding: Participants regained much of the weight they had lost after stopping, showing why long-term planning matters.

studies.meta: 2024 · McGowan et al. · Lancet Diabetes Endocrinol
studies.title: Once-weekly semaglutide 2.4 mg versus placebo in people with obesity and prediabetes
studies.finding: Greater weight reduction and more people returning to normal blood sugar at 52 weeks.

studies.meta: 2023 · Lincoff et al. · N Engl J Med
studies.title: Semaglutide and Cardiovascular Outcomes in Obesity without Diabetes
studies.finding: 20% relative reduction in major cardiovascular events in adults with heart disease and overweight or obesity, without diabetes.

studies.meta: 2023 · Kosiborod et al. · N Engl J Med
studies.title: Semaglutide in Patients with Heart Failure with Preserved Ejection Fraction and Obesity
studies.finding: Improvements in weight, heart-failure symptoms and physical limitations in obesity-related HFpEF.

studies.meta: 2024 · Perkovic et al. · N Engl J Med
studies.title: Effects of Semaglutide on Chronic Kidney Disease in Patients with Type 2 Diabetes
studies.finding: 24% relative reduction in major kidney events or cardiovascular death in adults with type 2 diabetes and chronic kidney disease.

studies.meta: 2025 · Sanyal et al. · N Engl J Med
studies.title: Phase 3 Trial of Semaglutide in Metabolic Dysfunction–Associated Steatohepatitis
studies.finding: Improved MASH resolution and fibrosis on liver biopsy at week 72.

studies.meta: 2024 · Bliddal et al. · N Engl J Med
studies.title: Once-Weekly Semaglutide in Persons with Obesity and Knee Osteoarthritis
studies.finding: Improvements in weight, knee pain and physical function compared with placebo.

studies.title: Impact of Semaglutide on Body Composition in Adults With Overweight or Obesity: Exploratory Analysis of the STEP 1 Study
studies.finding: Reductions in total fat mass and visceral fat, with a smaller decrease in absolute lean mass.

studies.title: GLP-1 medications in women with PCOS
studies.finding: Being studied where excess weight and insulin resistance are present. Semaglutide-specific evidence is limited, and it is not approved for PCOS.

studies.title: Inflammatory biomarkers during treatment
studies.finding: Some markers change during treatment. Semaglutide is not an established treatment for inflammatory or autoimmune disease.

studies.title: Mitochondrial function and PGC-1α
studies.finding: Mostly cell and animal research. It does not show increased mitochondrial energy production in patients.

studies.title: Low-dose or "microdosing" regimens
studies.finding: Not studied in large trials, so standard-dose results do not apply to them.

studies.title: Effects of semaglutide on kidney disease in type 2 diabetes: a randomized placebo-controlled trial
studies.studied: 106 adults with type 2 diabetes and chronic kidney disease, given weekly semaglutide or placebo for 52 weeks, with kidney scans and some biopsies.
studies.finding: The main kidney scan measures did not change significantly, but secondary results suggested less blood-flow resistance and slower scarring in the kidney with semaglutide.
studies.limit: The main goals of the trial were not met, and the possible benefits come from secondary measures in a small group.

studies.title: Efficacy and safety of once-weekly semaglutide 2·4 mg in Chinese adults with overweight or obesity (STEP 12): a randomised, double-blind, placebo-controlled, multicentre, phase 3b trial
studies.studied: 242 adults with overweight or obesity in mainland China and Taiwan, given weekly semaglutide or placebo plus lifestyle advice for 44 weeks.
studies.finding: Average weight loss was 12.1% with semaglutide compared with 2.2% with placebo, and stomach and gut side effects were the most common.
studies.limit: The trial lasted 44 weeks, was funded by the drug maker, and studied only Chinese adults, so results may differ in other groups.

sermorelin.name: Sermorelin
sermorelin.heading: Understanding the research behind growth hormone signaling
sermorelin.intro: Each entry says what was actually studied. Results from growth hormone replacement or other compounds don't mean sermorelin has the same effects.

studies.title: Growth Hormone Releasing Hormone Treatment in Normal Aging
studies.studied: Nightly GHRH(1–29), the sermorelin sequence, for 6 months in healthy older adults
studies.finding: IGF-1 rose (about 30% in men, 23% in women not on estrogen), lean mass rose and body fat fell about 5–8%.
studies.limit: Small studies. Physical function changes were equivocal and sleep quality didn't improve.

studies.title: GH-releasing hormone and GH secretagogues in normal aging: Fountain of Youth or Pool of Tantalus?
studies.studied: Review of GHRH and secretagogue research in aging
studies.finding: Summarizes effects on body composition, cognition and sleep, and why the evidence is limited.
studies.limit: A narrative review, not a new trial.

studies.title: Growth hormone releasing hormone improves the cognition of healthy older adults
studies.studied: 89 healthy older adults, daily GHRH vs placebo for 6 months
studies.finding: Better scores on selected tests, including problem solving and processing speed.
studies.limit: Selective improvements in a small trial. Not a treatment for cognitive disease.

studies.title: Effects of GHRH on cognitive function in adults with mild cognitive impairment and healthy older adults
studies.studied: 152 adults aged 55–87, tesamorelin vs placebo for 20 weeks
studies.finding: Favorable effects on selected cognitive measures. IGF-1 rose about 117%.
studies.limit: Tesamorelin is a different GHRH drug, not sermorelin. Not proof of dementia prevention.

studies.title: Growth hormone-releasing hormone and growth hormone secretagogues in normal aging
studies.studied: Review of human GHRH research, including sleep outcomes
studies.finding: Connects GHRH stimulation with body composition, cognition and sleep findings.
studies.limit: Highlights the lack of consistent sleep improvement.

studies.title: Growth Hormone and Aging
studies.studied: Age-related changes in GH physiology, plus GH and GHRH trials
studies.finding: A clinical overview of how the GH axis changes with age.
studies.limit: A reference chapter, not a sermorelin trial.

studies.title: Evaluation and Treatment of Adult Growth Hormone Deficiency: An Endocrine Society Clinical Practice Guideline
studies.studied: How adult GH deficiency should be diagnosed and treated
studies.finding: Confirmed deficiency needs proper testing, and is generally treated with recombinant GH.
studies.limit: About true deficiency, not wellness use.

studies.title: Hormones and Aging: An Endocrine Society Scientific Statement
studies.studied: Hormone changes with age, and the benefits and risks of hormone treatments
studies.finding: Notes that GHRH and GH secretagogues aren't approved as anti-aging treatments.
studies.limit: A scientific statement, not a trial.

studies.title: Effects of an Oral Ghrelin Mimetic on Body Composition and Clinical Outcomes in Healthy Older Adults
studies.studied: MK-677, an oral GH secretagogue, vs placebo in healthy older adults
studies.finding: Shown for broader GH-axis context only.
studies.limit: MK-677 is a different compound, not sermorelin.

studies.title: Determination That GEREF (Sermorelin Acetate) Injection Was Not Withdrawn for Reasons of Safety or Effectiveness
studies.studied: The regulatory history of the discontinued sermorelin product
studies.finding: The original Geref products weren't withdrawn for safety or effectiveness reasons.
studies.limit: Not proof that today's compounded sermorelin is approved or effective for wellness use.

mots-c.name: MOTS-c
mots-c.heading: The research behind MOTS-c
mots-c.intro: Each entry says who or what was studied. Animal and cell results don't guarantee the same effects in people.

studies.title: The mitochondrial-derived peptide MOTS-c promotes metabolic homeostasis and reduces obesity and insulin resistance
studies.studied: Cells and mice, including mice on a high-fat diet and older mice
studies.finding: MOTS-c activated AMPK, prevented diet-induced obesity and improved insulin resistance in mice.
studies.limit: Animal and cell data; not tested in people.

studies.title: The mitochondrial-encoded peptide MOTS-c translocates to the nucleus to regulate nuclear gene expression in response to metabolic stress
studies.studied: Cells and mice under metabolic stress
studies.finding: Under stress, MOTS-c moved into the nucleus and helped switch on protective stress-response genes.
studies.limit: About natural MOTS-c inside cells, not injections.

studies.title: MOTS-c is an exercise-induced mitochondrial-encoded regulator of age-dependent physical decline and muscle homeostasis
studies.studied: 10 healthy men (natural MOTS-c with exercise), plus mice of different ages given MOTS-c
studies.finding: Exercise raised muscle MOTS-c about 12-fold and blood levels about 1.6-fold; MOTS-c improved physical capacity in mice.
studies.limit: No people received MOTS-c; the human group was small and all male.

studies.title: Plasma and skeletal muscle MOTS-c levels in young, middle-aged and older men
studies.studied: Natural MOTS-c in men of different ages
studies.finding: Blood MOTS-c was lower with age, but muscle MOTS-c was higher in older men.
studies.limit: Measures natural levels only; shows links, not cause and effect.

studies.title: Mitochondrial-derived peptides in aging and healthspan
studies.studied: Review of MOTS-c and related mitochondrial peptides
studies.finding: Summarizes how these peptides relate to metabolism and aging.
studies.limit: A review, not a trial.

studies.title: FDA evaluation of MOTS-c-related bulk drug substances
studies.studied: Whether MOTS-c should be allowed as a compounding ingredient
studies.finding: FDA reported finding no human exposure data for compounded MOTS-c and raised immunogenicity and impurity concerns.
studies.limit: A regulatory review; an advisory committee later voted the other way.

studies.title: Enforcement Discretion Policy Regarding 503A Compounding Using Certain Peptide Bulk Drug Substances
studies.studied: Federal rules for compounding six peptides, including MOTS-c
studies.finding: Allows 503A compounding of MOTS-c when ten conditions are met, while FDA rulemaking continues.
studies.limit: Not FDA approval; temporary, and state rules may differ.

studies.title: MOTS-c on the WADA Prohibited List
studies.studied: Anti-doping status of MOTS-c
studies.finding: MOTS-c is listed as a prohibited AMPK activator, banned at all times for tested athletes.
studies.limit: Applies to athletes under anti-doping rules.

studies.title: Mitochondrial-derived peptides (MDPs) activated by physical exercise as therapeutic targets for metabolic disorders: A systematic review
studies.studied: 9 studies on exercise and mitochondrial-derived peptides, a group that includes MOTS-c and humanin.
studies.finding: Most of the studies reported a trend toward higher levels of these peptides after exercise.
studies.limit: Only 9 studies with different designs were included, few were in people, and results were not reported for MOTS-c on its own.

studies.title: Associations of Serum MOTS-c with Exercise Capacity and Antioxidant Markers in Young Males: A Cross-Sectional Study
studies.studied: 30 healthy young men aged 18 to 25: 10 elite athletes, 10 active men and 10 inactive men.
studies.finding: Blood MOTS-c levels were highest in athletes and lowest in inactive men, and higher levels went along with better fitness and antioxidant markers.
studies.limit: This small study measured people at one point in time, so it cannot show that MOTS-c causes better fitness.

studies.title: MOTS-c is associated with oxidative stress and arterial stiffness in peritoneal dialysis patients: a pilot study
studies.studied: 32 adults on peritoneal dialysis whose MOTS-c levels were measured in blood, urine and dialysis fluid.
studies.finding: MOTS-c levels in urine and dialysis fluid were linked to markers of oxidative stress and artery stiffness, in mixed directions.
studies.limit: This small pilot study only looked at links between measurements; it did not give MOTS-c to anyone.

bpc-157.name: BPC-157
bpc-157.heading: The research behind BPC-157
bpc-157.intro: Each entry says who or what was studied. Animal results don't guarantee the same effects in people.

studies.title: Emerging use of BPC-157 in orthopaedic sports medicine: a systematic review
studies.studied: 36 published studies: 35 in animals or cells, 1 in people
studies.finding: Consistent improvements in tendon, ligament, muscle and bone healing in animal models.
studies.limit: Almost all evidence is preclinical; well-designed human trials are lacking.

studies.title: Regeneration or risk? A narrative review of BPC-157 for musculoskeletal healing
studies.studied: Published research on benefits and possible risks
studies.finding: Describes promising repair effects alongside open questions, including the theoretical risk of promoting blood vessel growth in tumors.
studies.limit: A narrative review, not a trial.

studies.title: Intra-articular injection of BPC-157 for multiple types of knee pain
studies.studied: 16 adults with knee pain, injections into the knee joint
studies.finding: 14 of 16 reported meaningful pain relief.
studies.limit: Retrospective chart review with no control group; injection route differs from what we offer.

studies.title: BPC-157 for interstitial cystitis: a pilot study
studies.studied: 12 women with interstitial cystitis, injections into the bladder wall
studies.finding: 10 of 12 reported complete symptom resolution.
studies.limit: Very small, uncontrolled; route not offered here.

studies.title: Safety of intravenous infusion of BPC-157 in humans: a pilot study
studies.studied: 2 healthy adults given BPC-157 by IV
studies.finding: No side effects and no changes in heart, liver, kidney, thyroid or blood sugar markers.
studies.limit: Only two people; can't establish safety.

studies.title: Brain-gut axis and pentadecapeptide BPC 157: theoretical and practical implications
studies.studied: Review of animal research on the gut and nervous system
studies.finding: Summarizes animal findings on gut lining protection, NSAID injury and nerve protection.
studies.limit: Animal research, largely from one research group.

studies.title: Enforcement Discretion Policy Regarding 503A Compounding Using Certain Peptide Bulk Drug Substances
studies.studied: Federal rules for compounding six peptides, including BPC-157 acetate
studies.finding: Allows 503A compounding of BPC-157 for injection, oral or topical use when ten conditions are met, including single-ingredient products and documented absorption for oral forms.
studies.limit: Not FDA approval; temporary, and state rules may differ.

studies.title: Pharmacy Compounding Advisory Committee meeting, July 23-24, 2026
studies.studied: Whether BPC-157 and other peptides belong on the list of approved compounding ingredients
studies.finding: Committee materials review the available safety and effectiveness data for BPC-157.
studies.limit: A regulatory review, not a study.

studies.title: BPC-157 on the WADA Prohibited List
studies.studied: Anti-doping status of BPC-157
studies.finding: BPC-157 is prohibited at all times for tested athletes.
studies.limit: Applies to athletes under anti-doping rules.

studies.title: Human evidence for BPC-157 in orthopaedic and regenerative medicine: a systematic review of efficacy and safety
studies.studied: A review of all human studies of BPC-157 it could find; only 3 small studies with 30 people in total qualified.
studies.finding: The 3 studies reported symptom improvement in most people with no treatment-related side effects, but the reviewers rated the evidence as very low certainty.
studies.limit: The studies were small, mostly looked back at past records, and had no control group; the authors said BPC-157 should only be used in approved clinical trials.

tb-500.name: TB-500
tb-500.heading: The research behind TB-500
tb-500.intro: Each entry says who or what was studied. Watch whether a study used TB-500 or the full thymosin beta-4 protein, and whether it was in people or animals.

studies.title: Phase 2 trial of topical thymosin beta-4 gel for venous leg ulcers
studies.studied: 72 adults with venous leg ulcers, gel vs. placebo for up to 84 days
studies.finding: Complete healing: 33% on the middle dose vs. 24% on placebo; among those who healed, the middle dose healed about 40% faster.
studies.limit: Not statistically significant; a skin gel of the full protein, not TB-500.

studies.title: Study of thymosin beta 4 in patients with pressure ulcers
studies.studied: 72 adults with pressure ulcers, gel vs. placebo
studies.finding: Well tolerated, but no significant difference in complete healing vs. placebo.
studies.limit: Full-protein gel, not TB-500.

studies.title: Phase 1 single- and multiple-dose study of intravenous thymosin beta-4 in healthy volunteers
studies.studied: Healthy adult volunteers given IV thymosin beta-4
studies.finding: Well tolerated with no dose-limiting side effects.
studies.limit: Safety only; short-term; full protein, not TB-500.

studies.title: Thymosin beta-4 eye drops for dry eye: a Phase 2 trial
studies.studied: 72 adults with dry eye, eye drops vs. placebo
studies.finding: About 27% greater reduction in eye discomfort than placebo.
studies.limit: Missed its main goals; eye drops of the full protein, not TB-500.

studies.title: Thymosin beta-4 accelerates wound healing
studies.studied: Full-thickness skin wounds in rats
studies.finding: Thymosin beta-4 increased re-epithelialization and wound contraction and promoted new blood vessels and cell migration.
studies.limit: Animal study.

studies.title: Thymosin beta-4 and medial collateral ligament healing in rats
studies.studied: Rats with a torn knee ligament (MCL)
studies.finding: Treated ligaments healed with more organized collagen and better structure.
studies.limit: Animal study.

studies.title: Thymosin beta-4 activates integrin-linked kinase and promotes cardiac cell migration, survival and cardiac repair
studies.studied: Mice after a heart attack
studies.finding: Improved heart function and survival and reduced scarring.
studies.limit: Animal study; not a basis for treating heart disease.

studies.title: Enforcement Discretion Policy Regarding 503A Compounding Using Certain Peptide Bulk Drug Substances
studies.studied: Federal rules for compounding six peptides, including TB-500 acetate
studies.finding: Allows 503A compounding of TB-500 as a subcutaneous or intramuscular injection when ten conditions are met, including single-ingredient products.
studies.limit: Not FDA approval; temporary, and state rules may differ.

studies.title: Pharmacy Compounding Advisory Committee meeting, July 23-24, 2026
studies.studied: Whether TB-500 and other peptides belong on the list of approved compounding ingredients
studies.finding: The committee voted in favor of TB-500; FDA reviewers noted limited human clinical evidence.
studies.limit: A regulatory review, not a study.

studies.title: TB-500 and thymosin beta-4 on the WADA Prohibited List
studies.studied: Anti-doping status
studies.finding: Prohibited at all times for tested athletes.
studies.limit: Applies to athletes under anti-doping rules.

studies.title: Adjunctive recombinant human thymosin β4 therapy improves antibacterial outcomes against Staphylococcus aureus
studies.studied: Lab-dish tests of man-made human thymosin beta-4 on Staphylococcus aureus bacteria, alone and with antibiotics.
studies.finding: Thymosin beta-4 alone did little to kill the bacteria, but it boosted the effect of some antibiotics against free-floating bacteria.
studies.limit: This was a lab study only and was not tested in people; it had little effect on established bacterial biofilms.

bpc-157-kpv.name: BPC-157 & KPV
bpc-157-kpv.heading: The research behind BPC-157 and KPV
bpc-157-kpv.intro: Each entry says which peptide and who or what was studied. Animal results don't guarantee the same effects in people.

studies.title: PepT1-mediated tripeptide KPV uptake reduces intestinal inflammation
studies.studied: Intestinal cells and mice with colitis given oral KPV
studies.finding: KPV was carried into gut cells by the PepT1 transporter and reduced inflammation and tissue damage.
studies.limit: Cell and mouse study; not tested in people.

studies.title: Melanocortin-derived tripeptide KPV has anti-inflammatory potential in murine models of inflammatory bowel disease
studies.studied: Two mouse models of colitis
studies.finding: KPV reduced weight loss and gut inflammation in both models.
studies.limit: Animal study.

studies.title: Alpha-melanocyte-stimulating hormone and related tripeptides: anti-inflammatory and protective effects
studies.studied: Review of alpha-MSH, KPV and related tripeptides
studies.finding: Summarizes anti-inflammatory and protective effects in lab and animal models, including gut and skin.
studies.limit: A review of mostly preclinical research.

studies.title: KdPT, a related tripeptide, in mild-to-moderate ulcerative colitis
studies.studied: Adults with ulcerative colitis given KdPT, a lab-made relative of KPV
studies.finding: Tested tolerability and anti-inflammatory effects in people with UC.
studies.limit: KdPT is a different molecule; results don't apply directly to KPV.

studies.title: Lys-Pro-Val reduces fine-dust-induced inflammation in skin cells
studies.studied: Human skin cells exposed to fine dust
studies.finding: KPV lowered oxidative stress, cell death and inflammatory signaling.
studies.limit: Cell study only.

studies.title: Brain-gut axis and pentadecapeptide BPC 157: theoretical and practical implications
studies.studied: Review of animal research on the gut and nervous system
studies.finding: Summarizes animal findings on gut lining protection, NSAID injury and nerve protection.
studies.limit: Animal research, largely from one research group.

studies.title: Emerging use of BPC-157 in orthopaedic sports medicine: a systematic review
studies.studied: 36 published studies: 35 in animals or cells, 1 in people
studies.finding: Consistent improvements in tendon, ligament, muscle and bone healing in animal models.
studies.limit: Almost all evidence is preclinical; not about the gut.

studies.title: Safety of intravenous infusion of BPC-157 in humans: a pilot study
studies.studied: 2 healthy adults given BPC-157 by IV
studies.finding: No side effects and no changes in heart, liver, kidney, thyroid or blood sugar markers.
studies.limit: Only two people; can't establish safety.

studies.title: Enforcement Discretion Policy Regarding 503A Compounding Using Certain Peptide Bulk Drug Substances
studies.studied: Federal rules for compounding six peptides, including BPC-157 and KPV
studies.finding: Allows 503A compounding of BPC-157 (injection, oral, topical) and KPV (oral, topical) under ten conditions, including single-ingredient products only.
studies.limit: Not FDA approval; temporary, and state rules may differ.

studies.title: Pharmacy Compounding Advisory Committee meeting, July 23-24, 2026
studies.studied: Whether BPC-157, KPV and other peptides belong on the list of approved compounding ingredients
studies.finding: Committee materials review the available safety and effectiveness data.
studies.limit: A regulatory review, not a study.

studies.title: Lysine-Proline-Valine attenuates oxidized low-density lipoprotein-induced foam cell formation and inflammatory responses in RAW264.7 macrophages
studies.studied: Mouse immune cells (RAW264.7 macrophages) in a lab dish exposed to oxidized LDL cholesterol.
studies.finding: KPV reduced fat buildup and inflammation signals in the cells without harming them.
studies.limit: This was a cell study in mouse cells and was not tested in people.
